Keysight reported revenue of 1.85 billion for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54 percent from a year earlier and 7.51 percent above the quarter before [D1] [N]. Net income of 397 million rose 107.85 percent from a year earlier, and earnings per share of 2.82 came in against an estimate of 2.16 [D1] [N]. Communications Solutions Group revenue of 1.35 billion grew 43.09 percent and its operating income of 458 million grew 86.18 percent, while Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue of 501 million grew 21.6 percent and its operating income of 155 million grew 68.48 percent [D1] [N]. The company called the quarter a second consecutive record for orders and said orders rose sharply from a year earlier [D1]. For the fourth fiscal quarter the company guided revenue to 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion and earnings per share to 3.34 to 3.40, on a weighted diluted share count of 172 million [D1] [N].

The market's argument centres on how long the AI infrastructure build-out sustains the order growth, with management saying demand far exceeds what the company can supply and the order funnel at an all-time high [D3]. Management said supply chain will be the governor of near-term revenue for several quarters and described the supply situation as nonlinear, while analysts pressed on whether the order level is sustainable and on how much backlog may shift into the next fiscal year [D3]. Wireline revenue passed wireless revenue for the first time as AI data centre spending pulled demand for higher-speed optical transceivers, and the company said test intensity keeps rising as design margins shrink [D4]. An opinion piece linked from the call coverage argues that the AI growth is strong but that the valuation leaves little room for error [D3].

Management warned that one-time tariff impacts lifted fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, which raises the comparison that later periods have to clear [D3]. The fourth fiscal quarter revenue range sits only modestly above the revenue just reported, and analysts questioned that sequential step and asked for colour on the following year [D3]. Selling, general and administrative expense of 446 million grew 25.99 percent and research and development expense of 312 million grew 24.8 percent, so the cost base is rising quickly alongside the revenue [D1] [N]. Management also framed the 6G opportunity as larger than the 5G cycle, with customers moving into funded development programs [D4].

Management will take part in the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference on 2026-09-11 and in the 2026 Truist Technology Symposium on 2026-09-15, each with a fireside chat [D6]. The next report is due to cover the fourth fiscal quarter, for which the company guided revenue to 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion and earnings per share to 3.34 to 3.40 [D1] [N]. Management said it expects another record quarter for orders at a level consistent with the third quarter, supported by the highest monthly funnel intake [D4]. Management said integration of recent acquisitions is largely complete and that most of the cost synergy target should be realized on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year [D4].
